subject.title: [Feature]: Add a visible browser panel to the Control UI for login handoff and browser management

question: What security and ownership boundary should the browser login-handoff surface use before implementation?
rationale: The request is valid but exposes authenticated browser state and could land either as first-party Control UI, browser-plugin UI, or a generic plugin tab; automation cannot choose that product/security boundary safely.

options.title: Read-only-first operator panel
options.body: Add a secured browser handoff panel that shows status, tabs, target context, and screenshots/logs by default, with explicit gates for navigation, clicks, credential entry, submits, and resume.

options.title: Wait for plugin UI entry points
options.body: Defer browser-specific work until the generic plugin UI tab contract is accepted, then implement the browser panel as a browser-plugin-owned UI surface.

options.title: Defer the surface
options.body: Keep CLI/browser.request/headed-browser workarounds for now and leave browser-login handoff out of Control UI until this becomes a higher-priority product area.

recommendation.title: Read-only-first operator panel
recommendation.body: Add a secured browser handoff panel that shows status, tabs, target context, and screenshots/logs by default, with explicit gates for navigation, clicks, credential entry, submits, and resume.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from the canonical issue comment, recent Control UI sidebar/plugin-tab work, and browser.request history.
